why: Creep, compare, burst. The wall (gain 2.5, bias -3) senses; S1-S3 adapt it slowly and stably (tau 100, steep spokes 8 - 8 cos theta, bias -8, out -8 each, enough for light up to about 10). F (tau 3) and SL (tau 30) read the same front-blind sum with the same bias (-4, centred for far-field light), so F - SL is zero in steady light and positive when the light grew over the last ~30 ticks. R is a near-critical switch on 8 (F - SL) (self 4.3, bias -2.2: on above +0.08, off below +0.02). Its leaky resting output (~0.23) tilts the wall forward through R's spokes (-1.0 + 8 cos theta), so at rest the cell creeps ahead at ~2 R/tick, supplying the motion the comparison reads, and creeps faster as the comparison nears its threshold. When the light has been rising, R fires and the front half beats: a burst at ~8 R/tick. Q times the burst (tau 10, driven by R, cuts R off after ~8 ticks) and holds a short refractory while F and SL recover from the burst's own beats. H silences R in bright light (driven by the S's, the light level), so near the mouth the cell parks instead of creeping. Expected: B5-like runs toward light from far away, parking near the mouth, low cost at rest.
